claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

## Analysis for Alex (17 years old):

**Key Facts:**
- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex lives with you
- You live in the UK
- Alex has left education or training
- Alex has been registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services for **less than 20 weeks**
- Alex is not in local authority care
- Alex is not in hospital or residential accommodation
- Alex is not fostered
- Alex does not work 24+ hours/week
- Alex has not started an apprenticeship in England
- Alex does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

**Eligibility Assessment:**

According to the government guidance, for children aged 16 or over:
- "You'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training."
- **Crucially**: "You can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either: a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services"

Since Alex:
1. Is 17 years old (under 20) ✓
2. Has left education or training
3. Has registered with a government-sponsored careers service or armed services ✓
4. Has been registered for **less than 20 weeks** ✓
5. Lives with you ✓
6. Does not work 24+ hours/week ✓
7. Has not started an apprenticeship in England ✓
8. Does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right ✓

Alex meets the specific exception that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after leaving education/training, provided they are registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

## Good News! You ARE eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Why you're eligible:**

Even though Alex has left education or training at age 17, UK government rules allow Child Benefit to **continue for up to 20 weeks** when a 16 or 17 year old registers with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service, or
- The armed services

Since Alex has registered with one of these services and it's been **less than 20 weeks**, you still qualify for Child Benefit during this transition period.

**Important to note:**
- This eligibility will continue until the **20-week period ends** from when Alex registered
- After the 20 weeks, Child Benefit will stop unless Alex returns to approved education or training
- Make sure to keep the Child Benefit Office updated if Alex's circumstances change (e.g., if they start work for 24+ hours a week, begin an apprenticeship, or start receiving certain benefits in their own right)

If you haven't already claimed, you should apply for Child Benefit. If you're already receiving it, it should continue during this 20-week period.
